title: Farthest-Apart Neighbouring One Bits
statement:
Write the positive integer n in binary. Look at each pair of 1 bits that are next to each other in the list of 1 bits (no other 1 between them). Their distance is the difference of their bit positions.

Return the largest such distance, or 0 if n has fewer than two 1 bits.

examples.why: 37 is 100101. The 1 bits sit at positions 0, 2 and 5, so the neighbouring distances are 2 and 3.
6 is 110. Two touching 1 bits are 1 apart; the distance is not the number of zeros between them.
8 is 1000, a single 1 bit. The trailing zeros do not count as a gap.

hints: Walk through the bits from lowest to highest. What do you need to remember?
Remember the position of the last 1 bit you saw.
At each new 1 bit, the distance is its position minus the last position. Keep the maximum and update the last position.

explain.intuition:
The only state you need is where the previous 1 bit was. Shift n right one bit at a time, counting positions. Whenever the low bit is 1, compare its position to the previous one and remember the larger distance.

Starting with "no previous 1 yet" (for example -1) handles numbers with a single 1 bit: they never produce a distance, so the answer stays 0.
steps: While n > 0: if n & 1, then if last ≥ 0 update best = max(best, pos − last), and set last = pos.
Shift n right by one and increment pos.
pitfalls: Counting zeros between the ones, which gives 0 for 110 instead of 1.
Counting trailing or leading zeros as a gap for numbers like 1000.
Using >> on values at or above 2³¹ in JavaScript turns them negative. Here n ≤ 10⁹, so it is safe; >>> is the habit to build.

solutions.title: Binary string
solutions.idea: Convert to a binary string, collect the indexes of the 1s, and take the largest difference between neighbours.

solutions.title: Shift and track the last 1
solutions.idea: Read bits from the low end, remembering the position of the previous 1 bit.

followups: Return the widest gap for every number from 1 to n. Can you reuse answers?
Find the longest run of consecutive 1 bits instead. What changes in the loop?
